body:
Linear: https://linear.app/adebuild/issue/ADE-11/tabs-in-a-second-window-are-never-saved
Plan: `change-linear/plans/ade57-ade11-plan.md` section 5, PR 1 of 3.
Review rounds: 0

## Design approval

ADE-11 PR 1: no visible change, approved to go by General 2 m_inm2ypcusqd6 (2026-10-20)

## What changed

The window-transfer path is deleted. It was dead code.

- `src-tauri/src/window_transfer.rs` is deleted, with its `mod`, its `.manage(WindowTransferState)` and its two command registrations in `lib.rs`.
- `src/app/model/windowTransfer.ts`, its test and `windowTransferBootstrap.ts` are deleted.
- `loadBootWorkspace` loses its transfer branch, and `BootWorkspace` loses its `windowTransfer` field. `historyForCwd` had two callers, the transfer branch and the restore branch. It now has one, so it is inlined into `loadBootWorkspace`.
- `App` loses the `windowTransfer` prop and each place that read it. `main.tsx` stops passing it.
- The test mocks of `./windowTransferBootstrap` and the `take_window_transfer` handler in `tests/browser/app/backend.ts` are deleted.

## Why

The ADE-11 ticket names `if (windowTransfer) return` in App's snapshot save. That guard never ran.

- Nothing calls `stage_window_transfer`. On `069ac695`, `git grep -n stage_window_transfer` gives only `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:681` (the registration) and `src-tauri/src/window_transfer.rs:14` (the definition). It finds nothing in `src/`.
- `git log -S stage_window_transfer -- src/` gives `d730a6c7` (2026-09-02, "Drop Classic layout and the zen-mode toggle"). That commit removed the last `invoke("stage_window_transfer", ...)`.
- So `take_window_transfer` always answers null. `loadWindowTransfer()` always gives null, and every `windowTransfer` check in App is false.

This PR does not fix ADE-11. PR 3 does: it lets every window save its own row. This PR removes the dead path first, so PR 2 and PR 3 build on the real boot flow.

Data flow, before and after:

```
before  loadBootWorkspace: control_window_booted -> take_window_transfer (always null) -> loadResumedWorkspace -> App(windowTransfer=null, resumed)
after   loadBootWorkspace: control_window_booted -> loadResumedWorkspace -> App(resumed)
```

## How it was tested

Each run held the shared heavy lock for one command.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p monocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- `npx vitest run src/app/model/bootWorkspace.test.ts src/app/model/appLifecycle.test.ts src/app/model/appLifecycleRestore.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 25 of 25 pass. `bootWorkspace.test.ts` is the test file that calls `loadBootWorkspace`.
- `npx eslint` on the changed TS files passes.

Real-state proof: real saved data through the real code. I took a `.backup` copy of the live `com.monocode.second` `monocode.db` (read only). A scratch vitest (not committed) boots the real `loadBootWorkspace` against a writable copy of it. Only `@tauri-apps/api/core` is replaced, and each IPC command runs the SQL that `session_store.rs` runs against the copy. `take_window_transfer` answers null, as the real command does. The clock and `crypto.randomUUID` are fixed, so two runs on the same code give byte-identical output. I ran it on base `069ac695` and on this head, once for each history path in the loader: no recent project, recent project the same as the restored one, and a different recent project.

| Case | Restored tabs | Sessions | Active tab | History |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No recent project | 17, same ids and order | 33 | same | 9 rows, same |
| Recent = restored project | 17, same ids and order | 33 | same | 9 rows, same |
| Recent = other project | 17, same ids and order | 33 | same | 9 rows, same |

In each case the full boot result (`resumed`, `history`, `historyCwd`, the boot-time session upserts) is identical as JSON. The two differences are the expected ones: `BootWorkspace` no longer has the `windowTransfer` key, and the boot no longer calls `take_window_transfer`. To re-run: copy `change-linear/reviews/ade11-pr1-probes/zzAde11Boot.scratch.test.ts.txt` to `/tmp/mc947/ade11-pr1/harness.scratch.test.ts`, put a `.backup` of the DB at `/tmp/mc947/ade11-pr1/second.db`, make a base worktree at `/tmp/mc947/ade11-pr1/base`, and run `run.sh` from the same folder. The results are in `results.txt` there.

## Size

Non-test: +20 / -171 in 7 files. Test: +0 / -72 in 4 files.

## Review gate (self-check)

I ran thermo-nuclear and deslop on this diff. One finding, fixed: `historyForCwd` became a one-caller helper whose promise parameter existed only for the deleted branch, so I inlined it. Deslop found no slop. Two comments that named the window transfer are rewritten or removed.

- No new duplicate code. The diff only deletes code, apart from the inline.
- Non-test lines: +20 / -171, under 400.
- No function grew past the complexity limit. `loadBootWorkspace` lost a branch.
- No large file grew. `App.tsx` lost 15 lines and `appLifecycle.ts` lost 31.
- No new `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `any` or `#[allow]`.
- Typecheck and the boot tests pass.

## Risks

- No visible change. The removed code ran only when `windowTransfer` was set, and nothing could set it. New Window, restore and every save path behave as before.
- The `0.13.0` CHANGELOG entry mentions "windows transferred from another window". It is notes for a released version, so it is not changed.
- Out of scope, found on the way: `TabGroupMenu`'s "Move group to new window" item (`src/features/workspace/ui/TabGroupMenu.tsx:101-105`) never shows. Both callers pass `showActions={false}` (`src/app/shell/useProjectMenu.tsx:445`, `:532`) and `onPick={() => {}}`. It does not use the transfer code. It needs its own ticket.
title: ADE-11: remove the dead window-transfer path

body:
Change R v2, issue R5, part 1 of 2. Linear: [ADE-23](https://linear.app/adebuild/issue/ADE-23/r5-ask-and-ack-ledger).
Review rounds: 5

**Rebased onto `tyler/main` `a363d977` (#139 merged).** No code change in the rebase. `gate/integrity` against `a363d977`: `ok, 401 non-test lines changed`. `cargo test --lib -- ask_gate scenario:: mono_ control_cli:: session_store` on the rebased head: 410 passed. CI on `5eba0932`: 14 of 14 pass, `gate/integrity` included (`ok, 401 non-test lines changed`).



## Round 2 fix (`9fe5dbfd`)

The round-2 review found 0 blockers, 0 majors, 2 minors and 3 nits (nits in #151). This round adds a test only; `gate/integrity` is unchanged at `ok, 401 non-test lines changed`.

- **m1.** New test `a_retried_rejected_ask_gets_its_first_refusal`: an ask to an unknown target (`r5-nobody`) is rejected with `unknown_target`; the same call again under the same request id answers `unknown_target` with `duplicate: true`; no `mono_asks` row. With the rejected-repeat guard deleted (`Some(first) => {`), it fails: `left: (("unknown_target", false), ("request_id_reused", false))`. Clean, `ask_gate` and `scenario::asks` pass (7).
- **m2.** This body: the Proof mutation table (the transaction mutant is caught; the race text is gone), the data-flow block, the `decide_ask` line, the budget and open-ask counts, and both size mentions now match the head.
- Part 2 (`feat/ade-23-ack`) is rebased onto this commit and pushed as `a747d808` (17 `ask_gate` and `scenario::` tests pass); still no PR.

## Round 1 fixes (`977da383`)

The round-1 review found 0 blockers, 0 majors, 4 minors and 3 nits. Size: `gate/integrity` `ok, 401 non-test lines changed` against `f808e4af`. The fix commit is +203/-98 in 3 files. Part 2 (`feat/ade-23-ack`) is rebased onto this commit locally and pushed. It still has no PR.

- **m1.** New test `a_failed_ask_insert_leaves_no_carrier_row`. A temp trigger aborts the `mono_asks` insert. `asks::ask` returns the error and leaves no `mono_messages` row under that request id. Without the transaction, the carrier row stays, and the test fails (`m1_ask_skips_the_transaction`, caught). The earlier "race" explanation was wrong: every write goes through one `Mutex<Connection>`. What the transaction protects is the carrier and the ask landing together.
- **m2.** An ask whose request id already holds an accepted row that is not an ask (`is_ask`, a `mono_asks` lookup) is refused with `request_id_reused` and writes nothing. A repeat of a real ask, or of a rejected call, still answers its first outcome. Test: `an_ask_reusing_a_sends_request_id_is_refused`.
- **m3.** `decide_ask` takes plain `&Party` values. When the caller or the target has no saved row, `ask` skips the ask rules and lets the send gate answer: `unknown_caller`, `not_a_mono` or `unknown_target`. If the send gate lets such a row through (a Mono messaging a listed session with no saved row), the transaction is dropped and the answer is `not_direct_child`, with no row. Test: `an_ask_from_or_to_no_saved_row_gets_the_send_gates_answer`.
- **m4.** Budgets 9 and 481 are refused (`invalid_input`), and 10 and 480 are taken, in `an_ask_goes_only_to_a_direct_child_with_its_due_in_active_time`.
- **n1.** Fixed. The check is `due_minutes.is_some_and(|due| !range.contains(&due))`, and the hint is built from `DUE_MINUTES`.
- **n3.** Fixed. It fell out of m3's signature change: `decide_ask` returns `Result<Option<i64>, AskRefused>`, and `NewAsk` is gone. The levels come from `Party::level.rank()`.
- **n2.** Not a one-line change, so it is in #151 ("Nits from #150 (R5a)").

### Round 1 proof

**Reviewer files run under the fair lock** (each cargo run took `heavy-lock.sh` alone, through copies `r5-files/r5a-round1-run-fair.sh` and `r5a-round1-mutations-fair.py` that differ only in that prefix):

| Run | On the reviewed head `464c34c2` | On this head `977da383` |
|---|---|---|
| `r5a_send_then_ask_with_the_same_request_id` | `SEND accepted(dup=false)  ASK accepted(dup=true)`, `mono_asks rows: 0` (m2 confirmed) | `ASK request_id_reused`, `mono_asks rows: 0` |
| `r5a_unknown_caller_and_target` | `UNKNOWN CALLER send=unknown_caller ask=not_direct_child`, `UNKNOWN TARGET send=unknown_target ask=not_direct_child` (m3 confirmed) | `ask=unknown_caller`, `ask=unknown_target` |
| `r5a_a_failed_ask_insert_leaves_no_carrier` | passes | passes |
| `r5a_due_bounds` | `0, 9, 481, 100000` invalid, `10, 480` accepted, `GIGA DUE 5` invalid | same |
| `r5a_every_pair_of_levels` (file DB, then the `com.monocode.desktop` copy with 217 sessions and the `com.monocode.second` copy with 263) | exactly `giga->mono, giga->mono2, mono->lead, lead->worker` accepted on all three. Rows: Giga to Mono due NULL, the others due 3610000 | same on all three |
| PR tests plus probes, file DB | 8 passed | 11 passed |
| real copies | 2 passed each | 5 passed each |
| Reviewer mutations | 6 caught. `due_upper_bound_dropped` survived the PR tests (the probe showed 481 and 100000 accepted). `ask_skips_the_transaction` survived the PR tests, and the reviewer's fault probe failed under it. | The reviewer's anchors are old code, so the round-1 versions below replace them. |

**Round-1 mutations** (`r5-files/r5a-r1-mutations.py`, one lock per run): **6 of 6 caught**.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `m1_ask_skips_the_transaction` | `a_failed_ask_insert_leaves_no_carrier_row` |
| `m2_repeat_skips_the_ask_check` | `an_ask_reusing_a_sends_request_id_is_refused` |
| `m3_rowless_party_is_not_direct_child` | `an_ask_from_or_to_no_saved_row_gets_the_send_gates_answer` |
| `m3_let_through_rowless_target_is_accepted` | same |
| `m4_due_upper_bound_dropped` | `an_ask_goes_only_to_a_direct_child_with_its_due_in_active_time` |
| `m4_due_lower_bound_dropped` | same |

Also run: `cargo test --lib -- mono_ control_cli:: session_store` (400 passed), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `jscpd --fail-on-new-clones` (exit 0).

## Size and split

R5 as one PR was 576 non-test lines, over the 500 cap. It is split in two:

| Part | Branch | Contents | `gate/integrity` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1/2, this PR | `feat/ade-23-ask-ack-ledger` (`5eba0932`) | `mono_asks`, pure `decide_ask` and `is_direct_child`, `asks::ask`, `ask` dispatch through `mono_message_submit` | `ok, 401 non-test lines changed` against `a363d977` |
| 2/2 | `feat/ade-23-ack` (`53513cda`), pushed, PR opens after this merges (one PR in review per stack step) | `mono_ask_events`, pure `decide_ack`, `asks::ack`, `ack` dispatch, the 5 plan checkpoints | `ok, 212 non-test lines changed` against part 1 |

Part 1: +829/-48 in 8 files against `a363d977`. Non-test: `asks.rs` 255, `ask_gate.rs` 63, `mono_messages.rs` +47/-33 (the dispatch and the `submit_in` split), `lib.rs` 2, `session_store.rs` 1. The scenario files are under `tests/` and count as test code.

## What changed (part 1)

- **`mono_asks`** (`asks::ensure_tables`, called from `session_store::migrate` beside `active_clock::ensure_tables`): one row per key, as in plan section 2.
  - `id` is the id of the `mono_messages` row that carried the ask.
  - `parent_level` is 1 to 3, and `child_level = parent_level + 1`.
  - `state` is `open`, `acked` or `dropped`.
  - `due_active_ms` is NULL exactly when `parent_level = 1`, as a CHECK.
  - `paused_at_active_ms`, `stage 0..3` and `next_due_active_ms` are there for R8 and R14. They stay at their defaults here, since R8 owns the scheduler's input.
  - There are partial indexes on `next_due_active_ms` and `child_session` for open asks.
- **`ask_gate.rs`**, pure:
  - `is_direct_child(parent, child, started_by_parent)`: Giga to a Mono, Mono to a lead it started, lead to its own worker.
  - `decide_ask(&parent, &child, …)` returns `due_active_ms = active_ms + budget` (default 60 min, `due_minutes` 10 to 480), or `None` for a Giga. Otherwise it refuses with `not_direct_child`.
- **`asks.rs`**:
  - `ask` runs in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. It loads the facts from saved rows, decides, writes the carrier row through `mono_messages::submit_in`, and inserts the ask with that row's id.
  - The facts it loads: the caller's level (`monos.role`, or R4's `session_level`), the child's level, whether the parent Mono's accepted `start_session` row names the child, and the stored `mono_clock.active_ms`.
  - A repeat of the call (same request id) answers the first outcome and writes no second ask.
- **The carrier is an ordinary `send_message` row** (intent `new`, `wanting_reply` false) to the child. So an ask gets the send gate, delivery, the queue and dedupe exactly as a message does, and the 40-CHECK `mono_messages` table needs no rebuild. The `tool` column stays `send_message`, and `mono_asks` says which rows are asks.
- **`mono_messages.rs`** is dispatch only:
  - `submit` now opens the transaction and calls `submit_in(tx, …)`. The body is unchanged and is reused by `ask` inside its own transaction.
  - `submit_and_recheck` takes `impl Into<Call>`, so every existing caller passes its `Result<Input, String>` unchanged.
  - `mono_message_submit` maps the tool name through `asks::call`, which sends `ask` to `asks::ask` and the rest to `mono_gate::parse`.
  - `mono_row` became `pub(crate)`.
- **No UI, no CLI.** R6 adds the CLI and MCP tools and the rendering.

## Data flow

```
mono_message_submit(tool "ask") -> asks::call -> Call::Ask -> submit_and_recheck -> asks::ask
  due_minutes outside 10..480 -> invalid_input, no row
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE
    request id has a row:
      rejected        -> submit_in replays the first refusal (duplicate)
      accepted, an ask -> submit_in answers the first accept (duplicate)
      accepted, no ask -> request_id_reused, no row
    no row, both parties saved:
      caller_party, addressed_party, started_by, mono_clock.active_ms -> ask_gate::decide_ask
        refused -> not_direct_child, no row
    no row, a party unsaved: skip the ask rules; the send gate answers
      (unknown_caller, not_a_mono, unknown_target)
    submit_in(send_message to the child) -> carrier row (send gate, routes)
    new accept with saved parties -> INSERT mono_asks (id = carrier id, levels, due)
    new accept with an unsaved party -> drop tx (no row), not_direct_child
  COMMIT
```

## Proof

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `scenario::asks::an_ask_goes_only_to_a_direct_child_with_its_due_in_active_time`, file DB | passes. Giga to Mono: due NULL (with `due_minutes` 30 given). Mono to lead: due = stored `active_ms` + 60 min. Lead to worker: + 30 min. A repeat under the same request id is a duplicate. `due_minutes` 9 and 481 give `invalid_input`; 10 and 480 are taken. Giga to lead, a lead to another lead's worker, a worker to its lead and a Mono to a lead another Mono started all give `not_direct_child`. All 5 asks are still open after `down(60 s)`. |
| The same on a fresh `.backup` copy of `com.monocode.second` and of `com.monocode.desktop`, via `MONOCODE_SCENARIO_DB` | passes on both (first run 260 and 215 sessions; the round-1 rerun 263 and 217). The copies were deleted after each run. |
| `ask_gate` unit tests | `only_a_direct_child_can_be_asked`, `the_due_time_is_active_time_plus_the_budget_and_none_for_a_giga` |
| `cargo test --lib -- ask_gate mono_ control_cli:: session_store scenario::` | 406 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `jscpd --fail-on-new-clones` (vs `f808e4af`) | clean, exit 0 |

Mutations: the first four rows are from `r5-mutations.py` (round 0); the rest from `r5a-r1-mutations.py` (round 1) and the round-2 run. The ack rows are in the part 2 PR.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `a_giga_ask_gets_a_due` (the brief's "wrong due for level 1") | caught: `the_due_time_is_active_time_plus_the_budget_and_none_for_a_giga` |
| `due_ignores_the_budget` | caught: same |
| `a_mono_asks_any_lead` | caught: `only_a_direct_child_can_be_asked` |
| `a_lead_asks_any_worker` | caught: same |
| `ask_skips_the_transaction` | caught: `a_failed_ask_insert_leaves_no_carrier_row` (round 1). The transaction keeps the carrier and the ask row together. |
| request-id, rowless-party and budget-bound mutants | 5 caught, see the round 1 table |
| `r2_rejected_repeat_refused_as_reused` (the rejected-repeat guard deleted) | caught: `a_retried_rejected_ask_gets_its_first_refusal` (round 2) |

## Part 2 results (branch `feat/ade-23-ack`, for the record)

- All 5 plan checkpoints pass on a file DB and on both real copies: S1 ack reaches only the direct parent (worker to lead, lead to Mono, Mono to Giga); S1 a second ack is refused; S2 an ack of someone else's ask; S2 two acks at once; S4 a redo is a new key.
- `HEAVY_LOCK=… scripts/scenarios/repeat.sh asks::s2_two_acks`: `20/20 passed`.
- The brief's ack mutations: dropping `state = 'open'`, dropping `child_session` and skipping the ack transaction are all caught.

## Review gate

- **Self-pass.** I ran thermo-nuclear and deslop on the diff. Fixed:
  - The whole of R5 was over the cap, so it is split.
  - `ask` had two commit paths, now one.
  - A helper that only restated `caller_party(…).session` was deleted.
  - The carrier reuses `submit_in` instead of a second row writer, so there is no new insert code for `mono_messages`.
- **Duplication.** `npx jscpd . --baseline-from-ref f808e4af --fail-on-new-clones` exits 0.
- **Size.** 401 non-test lines (see the table above).
- **Complexity.** clippy is clean. `submit` got shorter, and `submit_in` is the old body.
- **File caps.** New files are `asks.rs` 220 lines and `ask_gate.rs` 170 with tests. `mono_messages.rs` grows by 14 lines.
- **Suppressions.** None added.
title: ADE-23 R5 (1/2): ask ledger

body:
Change R v2, issue R4. Linear: [ADE-22](https://linear.app/adebuild/issue/ADE-22/r4-levels-come-only-from-the-database).
Review rounds: 2

Size: 22 files, +823/-601 against `d29fea87` after round 1. `gate/integrity`: `ok, 334 non-test lines changed`. The round-0 split below is kept for reference.
- `gate/integrity`: `ok, 224 non-test lines changed`. App code: `mono_messages.rs` +65/-69, `mono_gate.rs` +44/-12, `control_cli.rs` +4/-1, the web app +6/-21, CHANGELOG and docs 1 line each.
- The World part (`tests/scenario/`) is +226: `s1_levels.rs` 166, `agents.rs` 59/8, `mod.rs` 1.
- The fixture shrinks by 113 lines because the copy fields are gone.
- `tests/browser/e7-session-callers.spec.ts` asserted the old copy fields. It now asserts that the caller and the `live` entries carry no `leadSessionId`.
- One concern, under about 400 lines, so no split.

## Round 2 fix (`f808e4af`)

The round-2 review found 0 blockers, 0 majors and 1 minor. The nits n6 to n10 are in #140. This round adds one test and no code. `gate/integrity` is unchanged: `ok, 334 non-test lines changed`.

- **m1.** New case in `e7-session-callers.spec.ts`, "a started worker whose save fails gets no prompt". The lead calls `sessions.start` and `session_upsert` throws for the worker id only. The lead gets `ok: false`, and `prompts(page, "app-lead-r1")` is `[]`.
- **Proof** (`r4-r2-mutation.sh`, under the lock, chromium):

  | Run | Result |
  |---|---|
  | clean | `10 passed` |
  | `a_started_turn_skips_its_save` (`access !== null &&` becomes `access === "operator" &&`, the reviewer's mutant) | `1 failed`: "a started worker whose save fails gets no prompt"; `9 passed` |

## Round 1 fixes (`923eb596`)

The round-1 review found 0 blockers, 1 major and 4 minors. The nits are in #140. The PR was rebased onto `d29fea87` (#130, #131). The only conflicts were the new `caller_role` fact and the Giga-row fixture cases, and both are kept. The fix commit is +309/-173 in 15 files. `gate/integrity` for the whole PR: `ok, 334 non-test lines changed`.

- **M1. Having app access now means having a row, decided where access is given.**
  - `submitAccess(blocks, typedOperator, startedBy, saved)` (`operatorCommand.ts`) gives no access to a session MonoCode never saves. `saved` is `mono || canPersistSession(session)`, and `canPersistSession` is the `~`, remote and ephemeral half of `shouldPersistSession`. A typed `/operator` there returns `"unsaved"`, and `submitSession` refuses it through the existing `/operator` status path. A later turn of such a thread gets `null`, so it runs with no app token.
  - A non-Mono turn with app access awaits `upsertSession(latest)` before its harness is called. A failed write fails the submit with the write's own error. This is the same await the steer path does, in the same function. No new path, effect or ref.
  - `acceptQuickLaunch` returns for an app launch (`startedBy`) only after `saveSession` of the new session succeeds. So the lead's `sessions.start` answers after the worker row exists.
  - The hint, the help line, `docs/agent-access.md` and the CHANGELOG line no longer say "send a message" or "new request id".
- **m3.** `unknown_caller` is now `Refusal::UnknownCaller`.
  - The pure `prelude` picks `not_a_mono` or `unknown_caller` from `caller.speaker` when the shell passes `caller: None`, as it already did for a Mono. `decide_reply` takes the caller for this.
  - `decide_action` refuses a session caller whose `caller_level` is `None`.
  - The two early returns, the hand-built `unknown_caller()` and `RejectCode::UnknownCaller` are deleted.
  - `app_help_names_every_level_code` now also covers `Refusal::ALL`, so the help names `not_a_mono` too.
- **m1.** I kept "an unsaved target is a lead", with a comment at both sites saying why it cannot be a worker: a worker's row exists before its lead's `sessions.start` answers. The `allowed` fixture case and the unused `ghost` session are deleted. The Rust test `check_action_reads_levels_only_from_stored_rows_and_none_for_a_mono` asserts the outcome.
- **m2.** The three doc comments now say the level comes from the stored row, and what a missing row means.
- **m4.** S1 runs the unsaved caller with `"access": "started"` and with `"access": "operator"` (cwd `~`), on `messages.send` and on `sessions.list`. Browser tests in `e7-session-callers.spec.ts` cover 1a (a first `/operator` turn whose save fails sends no prompt and shows the write error) and 1b (`/operator` in the `~` tab is refused and spawns no harness).

### Front end

**Waived by Tyler** (2026-10-20, via General 2, message m_i66xmoynjgfs): both strings approved exactly as written, option (a), no design step.

Two new user-visible strings. Both go out through existing paths, and there is no new UI element:
1. `Use /operator from a session in a project on this Mac. MonoCode does not save sessions outside a project.` This is a `status` event, the same path and style as the existing "Use /operator from a regular session turn, outside an orchestration run."
2. `MonoCode could not save this session, so the turn did not start.` This is a `session.error`, shown only when the save returns nothing for a session with access. A failed write shows the write's own error instead.

Agent-facing only (an app action error, not UI): `The workspace could not save the session yet.` from `acceptQuickLaunch`.

### Round 1 proof

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Reviewer's Rust home probe (`r4-round1-home-probe.rs`) at this head | `sessions.list -> Failed { code: "unknown_caller", hint: "MonoCode has not saved this session, so it cannot tell whether it is a lead or a worker. Only a saved session in a project on this Mac can use messages.* and app actions.", message_id: None }`. Rust still refuses a rowless caller. What changed is that such a caller can no longer get a token. |
| Reviewer's vitest probe plus `submitAccess` | `shouldPersistSession(home)` false. A typed `/operator` gives `unsaved` (refused). A later turn of the thread gives `null` (no app access). |
| `playwright test e7-session-callers.spec.ts composer-steer-turn-end.spec.ts --workers=1` | 22 passed |
| `vitest src/features/monos src/features/agent-app src/app/model src/features/sessions` | 2751 passed, 2 skipped |
| `cargo test --lib -- mono_ control_cli:: scenario:: approvals` | 339 passed (after the fixture rewrite) |
| Fixture writers (TS, Rust, TS) | `cmp` byte-identical |
| clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint on changed files, `jscpd --fail-on-new-clones` | clean, exit 0 |

Mutations (`r4-r1-mutations.py`, under the lock): **9 of 9 caught.**

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `an_unsaved_operator_caller_sends_as_a_lead` (the reviewer's mutant, on the new code) | `s1_levels_come_from_the_database_not_from_the_agent` |
| `an_unsaved_operator_caller_acts_as_a_lead` (app action path) | same |
| `an_unsaved_session_caller_gets_not_a_mono` | `a_session_caller_is_judged_by_its_stored_row_and_refused_without_one` |
| `decide_action_lets_an_unsaved_caller_act` | `check_action_reads_levels_only_from_stored_rows_and_none_for_a_mono` |
| `help_omits_unknown_caller` | `app_help_names_every_level_code` |
| `an_unsaved_target_is_a_worker` | `check_action_reads_levels_only_from_stored_rows_and_none_for_a_mono` |
| `an_unsaved_session_gets_app_access` (`submitAccess` ignores `saved`) | vitest "gives a session MonoCode never saves no app access, and refuses a typed /operator" |
| `a_first_access_turn_starts_before_its_save` | Playwright "a first /operator turn starts only once its session is saved" |
| `an_app_launch_answers_before_its_save` | vitest "answers an app launch only once the new session is saved" |

Before and after for the access decision:
```
before: submitAccess(blocks, typed, startedBy) -> operator | started | null; turn starts; first upsert fire-and-forget
after:  submitAccess(blocks, typed, startedBy, saved) -> unsaved (refused) | operator | started | null
        access && !mono -> await upsertSession(latest) -> sendHarnessTurn
        acceptQuickLaunch(startedBy): submit -> await saveSession(worker) -> answer the lead
```

## What changed

- **Rust is the only source of a session's level.**
  - `CallerArg` and `Speaker::Session` lose `leadSessionId`, and `LiveSession` loses `lead_session_id`. `CallerArg` keeps `deny_unknown_fields`, so a call that still names a lead is refused at the command boundary.
  - `AppActionCall` loses `targetLeadSessionId`, and `check_action` loses its `target_copy` parameter.
  - `session_level(conn, session)` reads only the `sessions` row. It returns `None` when there is no row. The copy leg is deleted.
- **`unknown_caller`.** A session caller with no `sessions` row is refused on both paths (`submit` and `check_action`), and no row is written. It is a new `RejectCode`, so the help test forced its help line. It has a hint, a `control_cli.rs` help sentence, a `docs/agent-access.md` line and a CHANGELOG line.
- **An unsaved target or recipient is a lead.** It has no stored lead link, so `recipient()` and `check_action` give it `SessionLevel::Lead`. This replaces "use the window's copy of its lead".
- **`Level::rank()`**: Giga 1, Mono 2, Lead 3, Worker 4. `Recipient::level()` maps a recipient to a `Level`. L6 is now `recipient rank < caller rank`. That is the old rule (a worker caller, or a Mono recipient) in one comparison: a lead or worker caller steering a Giga or Mono, or a worker steering its lead.
- **Web app.**
  - `levelGate(session, turnId)` drops its `leadOf` argument and no longer sends `targetLeadSessionId`. `callerOf` no longer sends `leadSessionId`.
  - The `Caller` type and `monoRoute`'s `live` list lose the field.
  - `App.tsx` no longer reads `sessionsRef` for a lead.
  - `agentApp.ts` sends no copy. It reads only Rust's answer (`leadSessionId` in `ActionChecked`), which comes from the stored row. No hook, effect, ref or state was added.

## Data flow

Before:
```
web app: session.leadSessionId (window copy) -> caller.leadSessionId, live[].leadSessionId, targetLeadSessionId
Rust: session_level(row, copy) = row ?? copy -> gate
```
After:
```
web app: caller {kind, sessionId, turnId, access, cwd}; live {sessionId, steerable, ownProject}; no lead field
Rust: session_level(row) -> Some(level) | None
  caller None  -> unknown_caller, no row
  target/recipient None -> Lead (no stored link)
```

## Proof

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| World S1 (`scenario::s1_levels`) | passes. A worker whose call names lead-b is refused at parse (`unknown field leadSessionId`). Without the claim it gets `worker_scope` to lead-b and is accepted to lead-a, its stored lead. After `down(60 s)` (kill and restart) it still gets `worker_scope`. An unsaved caller gets `unknown_caller` with no row on `messages.send` and on `sessions.start`. The row count is unchanged. Prints `4 sessions: 3 leads, 1 workers`. |
| Fixture writers | Both writers regenerated `appActionCheck.fixtures.json` (TS, then Rust, then TS again). `cmp` of the Rust write and the second TS write: byte-identical. 54 cases. The only reply change is the renamed R4 case: an unsaved target counts as a lead (`allowed`). |
| Fresh `.backup` copy of `com.monocode.second` (MonoCode 2) | `246 rows: 246 leads, 0 workers, 0 unparsable ids; unsaved id reads None` |
| Fresh `.backup` copy of `com.monocode.desktop` (instance 1) | `200 rows: 200 leads, 0 workers, 0 unparsable ids; unsaved id reads None` |
| `sqlite3` on the same copies | `count(*), count(lead_session_id)`: `246\|0` and `200\|0`, which matches the probe |
| `cargo test --lib -- mono_ control_cli:: scenario::` | 326 passed |
| `vitest src/features/monos src/features/agent-app src/app/model` | 857 passed, 1 skipped |
| `playwright test tests/browser/e7-session-callers.spec.ts --workers=1` | 14 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings` (workspace, all targets), `cargo fmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint on the changed folders | clean |

Neither real DB has a worker row yet, so the real copies prove the lead path and the `None` path. S1 and the unit tests prove the worker path. The probe was a throwaway test, and the copies were deleted after the run.

## Mutations

`r4-mutations.py`, run under the heavy lock: a clean run, then each mutation, with the file restored after each one.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `caller_may_name_a_lead` (copy leg back at the boundary: drop `deny_unknown_fields` on `CallerArg`) | caught: `caller_arg_parses_a_session_caller_and_refuses_mixed_combinations` |
| `submit_lets_an_unsaved_caller_act_as_a_lead` (drop the `unknown_caller` check in `submit`) | caught: `a_session_caller_is_judged_by_its_stored_row_and_refused_without_one` |
| `check_action_lets_an_unsaved_caller_act_as_a_lead` (drop it in `check_action`) | caught: `check_action_reads_levels_only_from_stored_rows_and_none_for_a_mono` |
| `unsaved_target_counts_as_a_worker` | caught: same test |
| `stored_lead_link_is_ignored` (`session_level` reads every row as a lead) | caught: `a_recipients_level_comes_only_from_its_stored_row` |
| `lead_ranks_below_worker` (swap ranks 3 and 4) | caught: `a_lead_steers_its_worker_by_the_start_row_it_wrote` |
| `l6_counts_a_peer_as_upward` (`<` to `<=`) | survived, equivalent. L6 never sees an equal-rank pair: a lead steering a peer lead gets `lead_scope` first, and a worker steering a peer worker gets `worker_scope` first. I confirmed the `lead_scope` reply with a throwaway assertion. |

6 of 7 caught. The survivor is equivalent, so no test can catch it.

## Review gate

- **Self-pass.** I ran thermo-nuclear and deslop on the diff. Fixed:
  - A stale `check_action` doc line still named `target_copy`.
  - A test assertion I added for the L6 peer case could not tell the mutant apart (see the table), so I removed it.
- **CI on the first push** (`17261d18`). `browser` failed on the two copy assertions above, and `gate/lint` failed on the jscpd clones above. Both are fixed in `119c58d1`.
- **Duplication.** `npx jscpd . --baseline-from-ref tyler/tyler/main --fail-on-new-clones` exits 0. The first push failed `gate/lint` with 2 new clones in `mono_messages.rs` tests. One was a store-seeding block I had copied. The other was an existing pair that became token-identical when `session_caller` lost its third argument. Both are now helpers (`fixture_store`, `lead_reports`). The first one also let me delete a `#[expect(clippy::too_many_lines)]` from the replay test.
- **Size.** `gate/integrity`: `ok, 224 non-test lines changed`.
- **Complexity.** clippy is clean. No new function over the limits, and `check_action` loses one argument.
- **File caps.** `mono_messages.rs` 10 442 lines (-4 code lines), `mono_gate.rs` 5 199 (+32 code lines, the `rank` and `level` impls). New `s1_levels.rs` is 166 lines.
- **Suppressions.** None added, one `#[expect]` removed.
title: ADE-22 R4: levels come only from the database

body:
Linear: [ADE-10](https://linear.app/adebuild/issue/ADE-10/turn-start-and-duration-wrong-when-a-queued-mono-message-runs-after-a)

## Why

A queued Mono message keeps its place in the chat when its turn starts, so a completion notice added after it can have started before it. `turnOpener` took the last opener by position and returned the notice. In the Fork Orchestrator chat this showed a turn that ran up to 29 minutes as 14 s, from a start 14 s too early, and the turn got no "Worked for" duration. ADE-7 and ADE-8 were reopened on this.

## What changed

- `turnOpener` (`session.ts`) returns the opener that started last, not the last one by position. It keeps `opensTurn`'s skips for steers, waiting queued messages and drafts. An opener saved with no start time still counts at its place, so a busy turn whose latest message has no time still shows no start (the existing ADE-7 test).
- `runningTurnOf` (`composerIntent.ts`) had its own "latest `startedAt`" loop. It now reads the turn id from `turnOpener`, and the loop is deleted. One rule decides the opener for all four readers.

Data flow, before and after:

```
before: blocks ─► turnOpener (last by position) ─► liveAgents, stampTurnDuration, runningTurnStart (ADE-5)
        blocks ─► runningTurnOf's own loop (latest startedAt) ─► composer bar
after:  blocks ─► turnOpener (latest startedAt) ─► liveAgents, stampTurnDuration, runningTurnStart (ADE-5)
                                               └► runningTurnOf ─► composer bar
```

## Scope

This PR changes no UI and nothing visible beyond the corrected times. `upsertKeyedStatus` (`apply.ts`) and the transcript's turn grouping (`transcriptActivity.ts`, `AgentTranscript.tsx`) do not call `turnOpener`. They keep their own rules and are not part of ADE-10.

## Tradeoffs

- **Why the untimed clause stays.** Without it, an older timed turn would beat a later message saved with no time. `liveAgents.test.ts` "does not take an older turn's start when the latest message has no time" would fail (mutation table below). For `runningTurnOf` the clause is new. Its old loop skipped untimed messages, so it could report an older turn's id while a later untimed message ran. It now reports the later message's turn id (usually none).

## Risks

- **The panel lists leads, not Mono chats.** The real case is in a Mono chat, which the live-agents rail does not list. A lead session gets queued Mono messages and notices the same way. The tests use a lead-style session built with the real `enqueueMonoMessage`, `appendUser`, `stopStreaming` and `acknowledgeMonoMessage`.
- **Equal start times.** Ties go to the later block by position, as `runningTurnOf` did.

## Blast Radius

`turnOpener` has three callers: `toLiveAgent` (`liveAgents.ts`), `stampTurnDuration` (`apply.ts`) and `runningTurnStart` (`projectReturn.ts`, ADE-5, used by `App.tsx` and `useWorkspaceNavigation.ts`). `runningTurnOf` has one caller, `SessionPane.tsx`. I found the callers with `grep`, because the LSP has no server for this repo. Every opener that is also the latest started, which is every turn except the inverted shape, gives the same block as before. The local run of the sessions, projects, monos and harness-core tests passes (202 files, 2601 tests).

## Verification

- **Tests from the real inverted shape.** Each test builds a finished turn, queues a message, runs a notice that is added after it and finishes first, then starts the queued message's turn:
  - `liveAgents.test.ts` "times a queued message's turn when a notice after it started first": start 5 000 while running, 4 000 ms when done. On tyler/main: `expected 4000 to be 5000`.
  - `apply.test.ts` "stamps a queued message's turn when a notice after it started first": durations `first 1000, next 4000, notice 500`. On tyler/main the queued message gets none.
  - `projectReturn.test.ts` "dates a queued message's turn when notices after it started first" uses the real rows' order (queued message started at 45, notices at 26 and 31, a steer). It opens that session, not one that started at 40. On tyler/main it opens the other one.
  - All three fail on tyler/main and pass here. `composerIntent.test.ts` already covered the same shape for `runningTurnOf` and still passes.
- **Real-state proof.** I took a `.backup` copy of `com.monocode.second`'s `monocode.db`. In a scratch worktree, a throwaway Rust test called the real `get_session_metadata` and `page()` behind `mono_session_get` and `mono_session_page(aroundBlockId)` on it. A throwaway vitest then loaded the Fork Orchestrator chat through the app's `getSession` and `getMonoTranscriptPage`, with only `invoke` answered from that output. It replayed each turn's blocks as they stood mid-turn and at the turn's end (the recheck's `asOf` rule and end bounds), on tyler/main's code and on this branch. Neither file is committed.

  | Real turn | | tyler/main | This PR |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `m_4kkwsmecdx`, started 08:03:45, ended by 08:33:13 | live-agent start | 08:03:31 | 08:03:45 |
  | | ADE-5 `runningTurnStart` | 08:03:31 | 08:03:45 |
  | | `stopStreaming` stamps | nothing | the message, 1 768 240 ms |
  | | live-agent duration | 14 161 ms | 1 768 240 ms |
  | `m_ghsv7ogxwg`, started 20:26:05, ended by 20:26:33 | live-agent start | 20:26:00 | 20:26:05 |
  | | ADE-5 `runningTurnStart` | 20:26:00 | 20:26:05 |
  | | `stopStreaming` stamps | nothing | the message, 28 459 ms |
  | | live-agent duration | 5 206 ms | 28 459 ms |

  The durations use the recheck's upper bounds for each turn's end. The real end is at or before them, so the real duration is at most 29 min 28 s and 28 s.
- **Mutations** (`turnOpener` broken one way at a time, four test files run):

  | Mutation | Failing tests |
  | --- | --- |
  | Pick by position again | the 3 new tests and `composerIntent`'s "reads the running turn from the opener that started last" |
  | Rank by start time only, with untimed openers never winning | "does not take an older turn's start when the latest message has no time" |
  | Pick the earliest start | 7 tests, the 3 new ones among them |

- **CI on `58bddd6c`:** all 14 checks pass, `gate/lint` and `gate/integrity` included (`integrity: ok, 50 non-test lines changed`).

## Size

5 files, +98 / -23. Non-test: +27 / -23 (`session.ts` +16 / -4, `composerIntent.ts` +11 / -19). Test: +71. `gate/integrity` locally: `ok, 50 non-test lines changed`.

## Review

Review rounds: 0.

I ran the thermo-nuclear and deslop passes on the diff. They removed `runningTurnOf`'s copy of the rule instead of keeping it beside the new one. Nothing else needed a change.
title: ADE-10: pick the turn opener by start time, not position

body:
## Why

A Mono groups every session that one of its turns monitors. The group sent nothing until its slowest member stopped, so one long session held every other result. On 10-19 this delayed the ADE-8 review r1 notice by 52 min and the #93 fix r1 notice by 30 min. It held four 18:22 results for 41 to 49 min behind a gate builder that ran until 19:27.

## What changed

- `MonoSessionCompletionBatches` gives each group a phase: `turn`, then `hold` for 60 s after the launching turn ends, then `open`. The pure function `releasableResults` decides what each group sends now. In `hold` it sends only when every member has stopped. In `open` it sends every ready result. Each result leaves the group when it is sent, so it is sent exactly once.
- The 60 s wake uses `scheduleAfter`. This is the app scheduler that the Giga turn guard already used, moved out so both can call it. No new effect, polling or copied state.
- The Mono instructions, the multi-session notice text, the `sessions.start` CLI help and CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` state the new rule. `MONO_PROMPT_VERSION` goes to 29 so live chats get the new rule.
- A delivery has its own type, `{ monoId, results }`. `dismissSession` removes the session from in-flight deliveries and releases only groups.

Data flow, before:

```
member stops -> settle -> release: turn ended AND every member stopped? -> one notice
turn ends    -> closeInactive  -> release (same gate)
```

Data flow, after:

```
member stops -> settle        -> release -> releasableResults(results, phase) -> notice of ready results
turn ends    -> closeInactive -> phase = hold, scheduleAfter(60 s) -> release (same function)
60 s later   -> phase = open  -> release (same function)
```

## Scope

- Covered: when results are sent after the launching turn ends. Results that stop during the turn, or within 60 s after it, still arrive as one notice.
- Left out: groups live only in memory, so a relaunch while a group waits drops it. This is ADE-46 (change R, R8 outbox).
- Left out: a sessions.send that steers a turn an earlier group already watches reports that turn once per request. tyler/main does the same (seq 1892 and 1914). The fifth timeline pins it, and a ticket follows.

## Blast radius

This changes only when queued completion notices reach the Mono. Delivery, the queue and dismissal stay the same. A Mono can now get several notices for one turn, and its instructions now say so.

## Verification

- Real-state proof (real saved data through real code). `monoCompletionTimelines.test.ts` replays five timelines from a `.backup` copy of the MonoCode 2 database (`com.monocode.second`, taken 10-19 19:40). Each group goes through the real `MonoSessionCompletionBatches` and `enqueueMonoSessionCompletion`, with the launch, Mono idle and member end times. `ade15-evidence.py` on that copy confirms the three ticket timelines. It also shows that the gate builder `30f5be8b` ended at 19:27:31 and released all five 18:22 results in one notice at that second. The fourth group (Mono `…e9ff464c`, 10-19 09:46) has the long-runner shape. `6918d65a` stopped during the turn, and `4abb60aa` ran 38 min after it. The fifth timeline covers the `sessions.send` entry point: group 1790 with group 1839 (Mono `…05cb6cb4`, 19:16), whose three sends include one that steers `30f5be8b` while group 1790 still watches it (fresh `.backup` at 20:24).
- On tyler/main all five replays fail. The received notices match the database exactly, including seq 1892 (19:27:31) and seq 1914 (19:52:39) for the fifth. With the fix, each member reaches the queue when it stops. `6918d65a` arrives at 10:11:58, 60 s after the turn ends, and `4abb60aa` arrives alone at 10:49:03. In the fifth, `7a1eab69` and `4d93f1f2` arrive at their own ends.
- `npx vitest run` on the five changed test files plus `gigaTurnGuard.test.ts`: 70 passed. On tyler/main sources the new and rewritten tests fail (8 failed). Eight mutations of the fix are each caught. Examples: the old hold-until-all rule, no hold, a hold 1 s short, no scheduled wake, ignoring acceptance, keeping sent results, and a dismissal that skips deliveries in flight. `tsc --noEmit` passes.

Tests that changed:

- New, `real Mono completion timelines`: ADE-8 review r1, #93 fix r1, the four 18:22 launches with gate builder `30f5be8b`, `6918d65a` with long runner `4abb60aa`, and "sessions.send group 1839 steers 30f5be8b while group 1790 still watches it".
- Rewritten, because they pinned hold-until-all: "waits for the launching turn, then sends results that stop within the hold together", "sends failures and cancellations when the hold ends, then a later result alone", "keeps later requests and other Monos independent of a slow earlier group".
- Made explicit about the hold: "queues one consolidated report behind chat and never steers a busy Mono", which now checks that a 59.999 s end merges into one notice of 2. Added "sends an accepted sibling when the hold ends, then an undecided submission once accepted". "releases an accepted sibling when an undecided submission is rejected" holds as written, because its events fall inside the hold.

## Size and review gate

- Size: 10 files, +384 / -83. Non-test: 5 files, +94 / -58 (one of them is the CHANGELOG line).
- Thermo-nuclear and deslop self-pass, again on the round 1 diff. Round 1 change: a delivery has its own type, which removes `result.value!` and the `release` calls on deliveries. Changes after the pass: the decision function returns entries, which removes a non-null lookup. `closeInactive` has one branch instead of two `ending` checks. A comment that only restated a signature is gone. The `closed` flag and the stored batch id are gone, because the phase and a per-delivery id replace them.
- Duplicates: jscpd with the gate config and `--baseline-from-ref tyler/tyler/main --fail-on-new-clones` exits 0.
- Complexity and suppressions: ESLint with the gate config (#103) over the changed files reports 63 problems on base and 63 on head, all old debt. Round 1 files: 0 problems. No new `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `any` or `#[allow]`.
- File size: no file crosses its cap. `monoSessionCompletion.ts` has 362 lines, and `App.tsx` gains 3 net lines.
- Typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passes. Scenario tests: listed above.
